newsitem.title: USA: Group urges Congress to probe Elk Hills field sale.
newsitem.headline: Group urges Congress to probe Elk Hills field sale.

text.p: Consumer advocates Thursday urged Congress to investigate the Energy Department's handling of the sale of its Elk Hills oil and gas field in California.
Under law, the department is required to sell its 78 percent stake in field, the 11th largest in the lower 48 states, by February 1998 and is scheduled to start seeking bids next month.

In letters to the leaders of Senate and House committees in charge of the Elk Hills field, consumer group Citizen Action called for a probe on whether the Energy Department was undermining efforts to get the best price for the field.

"We believe that the Department of Energy is not carrying out its reponsibilities under the law and that certain political appointees in the Department are deliberately sabotaging efforts to obtain maximum value for the public's property," the letter from Edwin Rothschild said.

"We urge you to investigate the Department to determine ... whether the Department is actively undercutting and subverting congressional intent," said Rothschild, energy policy director of Citizen Action.
Rothschild has long fought the planned sale, saying it would amount to a massive loss to taxpayers, because oil and gas sales from the field net the government about $200 million annually.
